## Exact assumptions and conditional bounds

- [`sat26-general`](../../ASSUMPTIONS.md#sat26-general)
- [`sat26-reported-formal`](../../ASSUMPTIONS.md#sat26-reported-formal)

Conditional on `sat26-general`:

$$
2^{O(n\log\log n/\sqrt{\log n})}L^{O(1)}
$$

Alternatively, conditional on `sat26-reported-formal`:

$$
2^{O(n(\log\log n)^2/\sqrt{\log n})}L^{O(1)}
$$

The resulting algorithm is deterministic and uses polynomial space, conditional on the corresponding assumption and this derivation. $L$ denotes the original input length; constants may depend on the stated fixed constants. Logarithms in asymptotic bounds may be regularized when the declared measure is small.

## Preprocessing

Use the entire input graph; no kernel is required. Enumerate all forbidden-copy vertex sets in n^{O_H(1)} time. The empty input has optimum zero and the empty witness.

## Encoding size

| Quantity | Bound |
| --- | --- |
| Boolean variables, including auxiliaries | $O(n)$ |
| Clauses | $O_{\mathcal H}(n^h+n)$ |
| Maximum clause width | $\max\{h,3\}$ |

## Derivation

1. Use one deletion bit per vertex and the clause $\bigvee_{v\in S}x_v$ for each forbidden-copy vertex set S. A deletion set is feasible exactly when it meets all these copies, since vertex deletion does not change adjacency among survivors.

2. For a threshold b in [0,n], add $\sum_v x_v\le b$ with the O(n)-size cardinality circuit. Each query has N=O(n), M=O_H(n^h+n), and width at most max(h,3), including every auxiliary variable. Its bit length is O_H((n^h+n) log(n+2)).

3. Threshold feasibility is monotone in b. Deleting all n vertices is feasible because every forbidden graph is nonempty. Binary search uses O(log(n+1)) fixed-width SAT queries to find the optimum b*. This is a direct satisfiability reduction; no signed-count cancellation is needed.

4. Keep the optimum threshold and fix the original deletion bits one at a time. Test x_v=0 while keeping previous choices; retain zero if satisfiable and otherwise force one. This uses at most n further queries and O(n) unit clauses. The resulting set is feasible and has minimum size b*.

5. Polynomially many sequential general-density SAT calls give A(n)L^{O(1)} time and polynomial space. The separately reported formalization assumption supplies the alternative stated bound. Optimum solution counts belong to the paired counting entry.

## Caveats and comparison limits

- The original vertex count n is the scale. A solution-budget FPT bound requires a separate variable-reduction argument.
- The forbidden family and copy convention must remain fixed. The clause width can be greater than three but is constant; apply the corresponding fixed-width SAT statement directly.
- This is vertex deletion, not edge modification, forbidden-minor deletion, or binary-weight optimization. No latest-best-algorithm comparison is claimed.

The derivation must preserve the objective and account for the encoding length of numerical values; a decision consequence alone does not establish the stated optimization bound.
